Radiation
Radiation therapy (RT) alone is the most common treatment 
for certain types of head and neck cancers, such as cancer of 
the nasopharynx, larynx, and oropharynx.36, 37 Radiation may be
used to cure the cancer, as in Hodgkin’s disease, testicular semi-
nomas, thyroid carcinomas, localized cancers of the head and 
the human body that are susceptible to the eﬀ ects of these 
lethal agents include those that are frequently dividing, such 
as the cells of the bone marrow (red blood cells, white blood
cells, and platelets), the epithelial lining of the gastrointesti-
nal tract, and the cells of the hair follicles. Th e most common
